headline: Contracts flow. Budgets swell. Startups thrive.
deck: This week saw significant contracts and funding in the space sector, highlighting a robust market landscape.

stories.head: Viasat bags $307 million Marine Corps contract
stories.body: Viasat has secured a $307 million contract with the Marine Corps for satellite communications, further entrenching its role in military connectivity. This deal is part of a broader trend where defense budgets are increasingly allocated towards advanced communications systems. With military needs evolving, Viasat is positioning itself as a go-to provider in a competitive field.
stories.soWhat: As military operations become more reliant on connectivity, Viasat's contract could signal a shift in how defense budgets prioritize communication technologies.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris team for SDA constellation
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris have joined forces to bid on a tactical Space Development Agency (SDA) constellation project, showcasing a strategic alliance in the defense space. This collaboration is indicative of a growing trend where companies are pooling resources to tackle complex government contracts, especially in the realm of space-based technologies. The stakes are high, with the SDA's focus on enhancing national security through advanced space capabilities.
stories.soWhat: This partnership reflects a shift towards collaborative approaches in defense contracting, as companies realize that solo efforts may not cut it in the face of stringent government requirements.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M, eyes co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has successfully closed a $190 million Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding will bolster its efforts in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, areas that are increasingly critical as geopolitical tensions rise. The investment underscores a strong belief in the need for enhanced security measures in space, reflecting a broader market trend.
stories.soWhat: True Anomaly's funding highlights the growing recognition that space security is not just a niche concern but a fundamental aspect of national defense strategy.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on ESA and JAXA
watchlist.body: The finalized agreement on the Apophis mission could set the stage for future international collaborations on planetary defense.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's next moves post-review
watchlist.body: With the Dream Chaser variant clearing its critical design review, the next steps will be crucial for its timeline and market positioning.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension implications
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension on the TITAN program may signal a deeper commitment to integrating advanced data solutions in military operations.

watchlist.title: Watch for GPS jamming trends
watchlist.body: The return to pre-2024 levels of GPS jamming in the Eastern Med could impact operational strategies for both military and commercial entities.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
